newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African hears eulogies to die for.
newsitem.headline: S.African hears eulogies to die for.

text.p: Talayi George Sogcwe sat up in his coffin and brought his funeral service to an abrupt end.

Two hours into the sombre service at his home in the Port Elizabeth black township of Zwide at the weekend, Sogcwe, 65, had heard enough of the eulogies of his friends to know that they loved and admired him.
"I simply wanted to know what people would say about me when I am dead," he told the Eastern Province Herald.
"I am satisfied they spoke the truth about me and not lies, as is often the case when a person is dead."
Sogcwe staged the mock funeral with the help of his wife and family at a total cost of over 5,000 rand ($1,064), which is more than twice the average monthly income of a Zwide family.
He said he would keep the coffin for his real funeral.
